feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The candidate matches the iteration 5 design exactly (kp 2.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, search_right, sensor weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], sensors at x = -0.04, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.04 with y = 0.05, sensor_size 0.012, 12 cm track, 3 cm radius, 16 cm body, 12 cm width, 0.8 kg). Iteration 5 is the best raced design at 75.779. Every single-field departure from it has lost score: kp 1.6 gave 51.18 (iteration 6), sensor_size 0.016 gave 60.12 (iteration 7), kd 0.2 gave 69.03 (iteration 8), and base_speed 1.1 gave 51.33 (iteration 9). Iteration 4 showed that kp 2.5 lowers progress on every track, so kp 2.0 stays. Iterations 2 and 3 show base_speed 1.0 is a trade-off: it raised oval progress (0.115 to 0.209) and lowered the bend tracks. The candidate is valid and not obviously broken, and it is a banking step. Its race should reproduce about 75.8, which secures this iteration's score. It will not add new information about the failure. All races, including iteration 5, end with one line-loss event and max_error of about 0.062 to 0.067 m, above the 0.06 m limit, with low oscillation (0.08 to 0.16). The failure is a slow drift to one edge. Read the next race this way. (1) If the score is about 75.8 and max_error and line_loss_events match iteration 5, the design is reproduced and is the base for the final iteration. (2) If the score is clearly different from 75.8, the run is not deterministic and the difference should be noted before any further change. Because only one iteration remains after this one, the next revision should be a single, well-motivated test of an untried lever, not a repeat of the iteration 6 to 9 changes.
